cases.evidence: Fresh-load Tab walk (puppeteer, no body-tabindex seeding) gives the true document order: stop1 button tabindex=1 'Share on Facebook' y=904, stop2 tabindex=2 'Share by email' y=904, stop3 tabindex=3 'Share on X' y=904, stop4 tabindex=4 LinkedIn y=904, stop5 tabindex=5 'Copy link' y=904, THEN stop6 'CI cache guide' y=408, stop7 'sharding doc' y=563, stop8 'affected-targets walkthrough' y=691, stop9 'rollout notes' y=788, stop10/11 related links y=1003/1040. So the first Tab from page load lands on a footer share button and focus then jumps back up to the article body. (Note: eval/act-augmented/_tools/probe-case.js sets body tabindex=-1 and focuses it before tabbing, which SKIPS the positive-tabindex group entirely - it reported only the 6 natural-order links and never showed the buttons.)
cases.reasoning: Davin's observation is factually correct and reproducible: positive tabindex 1-5 hoists the whole share row (page bottom, y=904) ahead of every link in the article (y=408-788), so the traversal really does go down, back up, then down again - not merely scrambled within the row. The corpus rationale only defends the WITHIN-ROW order ('five independent share actions, order carries no meaning') and the .md's claim that 'the scrambled order is confined to the order-irrelevant share row' / 'the meaningful content flow is untouched' is not true of the global document order. Whether that global displacement 'affects meaning or operability' (F44) or still falls under the Trusted Tester social-icons Does-Not-Apply note is a genuine ground-truth judgment, and repairing it would flip expected from inapplicable to failed.

cases.evidence: p#bestinterest's only DOM text is 'Where else would you find a better interest rate?' (line 66); the rate lives solely in the stylesheet: background: url('data:image/svg+xml...<text ...>19.3%25 APR</text><text ...>Typical Variable</text>') (line 37). Screenshot confirms a green badge reading '19.3% APR / Typical Variable' rendered left of the question, with no equivalent anywhere in the DOM. No img/svg/role=img/object element exists on the page.
cases.reasoning: This is WCAG F3 Example 1 reproduced verbatim: load-bearing information (the APR) is carried only by a CSS background-image, which generates no accessibility-tree node and can take no text alternative. Mengqi filed 'no-error' with an empty comment and no specifics; Ajit approved. Verified myself against the source and a rendered screenshot - the failure is real and the expected='failed' label is correct.

cases.evidence: Every atom circle is paired with an in-sphere <text> number (1 x2 carbon, 2 x2 oxygen, 3 x4 hydrogen, lines 55-70); the legend gives colour AND number ('1 Carbon (1)', '2 Oxygen (2)', '3 Hydrogen (3)', lines 74-76); the three questions reference atoms by number ('atoms labeled 2 (oxygen)', 'element number of the topmost atom'). Screenshot confirms the numbers are legible inside each sphere; the svg also carries role=img with a descriptive aria-label.
cases.reasoning: Element identity travels on two independent channels (hue and printed number), so colour is not the sole visual means and 1.4.1 is met - expected='passed' is correct. Both annotators answered issueExists='no' and therefore agree with the corpus; Mengqi's contentless 'no-error' comment reports no defect in the case itself.

cases.evidence: Puppeteer run of the real dialog flow: open on 'payments' -> focus '#rm-cancel'; confirm -> focus button.x aria-label='Remove label needs-repro' (the next chip) with chips now [bug, needs-repro, p1]; delete the LAST chip p1 -> focus falls back to 'Remove label needs-repro' (the previous, now-last chip); Escape on the 'bug' dialog -> focus returns to 'Remove label bug' (chip survives); after deleting every chip -> focus lands on button.addlabel '+ Add label'. All four branches match confirmRemove() at lines 132-146 and the corpus mechanism exactly.
cases.reasoning: The page behaves as documented and expected='passed' is correct; Ajit himself answered issueExists='no', so he does not dispute the label. His complaint is about the annotation platform, not the page - and it is partly grounded: eval/act-augmented/_annotator/index.html renders c.mechanism and c.whyMiss (whyAutomatedToolsMiss) into #mechBox/#whyMissBox on the Decide step, so annotators read rationale prose that literally says 'Judging it a PASS requires...'. That is an IRR-instrument problem (the rationale leaks the expected answer into the judgment task), not a defect in this test case.

cases.reasoning:
Davin approved with issueExists='no' and his comment is a confirmation, not a complaint - and it is right: the page is a correctly built passing control for summary-vs-state reconciliation. Separately worth noting (not a complaint, and not the annotator's point): the served page still contains a visible
'Why this page passes (and why it is the control)'
block that states the answer in rendered body text, which the HTML-comment strip did not remove.

cases.evidence: Probe of the Save flow: mutation sequence in the live region is 'Draft' -> class 'savestate saving' + text 'Saving' -> class 'savestate saved' + text '' (empty). After the save settles, saveState.textContent === "" and getComputedStyle(#saveState,'::after').content === '" \u2713"'. The element is <span id="saveState" class="savestate" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"> - it has NO role="status", and after save it holds no text alternative of any kind; the only 'Saved' signal is the CSS-generated green check.
cases.reasoning: Davin's comment claims 'the status role is provided and text alternative' - both halves are wrong: there is no role=status (only aria-live=polite), and the saved state carries no text at all after the class flip. His Q1 answer (issueExists='yes') actually agrees with expected='failed', so he is not contradicting the label. One caveat for the record: my CDP AX dump does expose a StaticText '\u2713' node, so the strongest form of the rationale ('CSS generated content is not exposed') overstates current Chromium behaviour; the outcome still holds on the robust argument (a bare check glyph is not the status 'Saved', and a polite region whose final mutation empties its text announces nothing useful).

cases.evidence:
result.json case-04 describes a 'Higher-ed LMS essay editor ... wired role=alert (assertive)' with primarySelector 'span#autosave[role="alert"]'. Runtime probe of the shipped page: document.querySelectorAll('[role=alert]').length === 0 and document.getElementById('autosave') === null; the region is

. At load aria-live='off' (applyFocusMode(true), line 90, with button#focusToggle aria-pressed='true'); after clicking #submitBtn the region still reads aria-live='off' while holding 'Refill request FAILED: Warfarin 5 mg requires prescriber re-authorization...'. Mutation log shows the aria-live='off' attribute set first, then the failure text injected into the muted region. case-04.md already documents this correctly ('backwards SCR14', F103, p#refillStatus).
cases.reasoning: Davin is exactly right: the shipped page's defect is that no politeness is in effect at all (aria-live='off'), not that the politeness level is too assertive. The result.json row's scenario, mechanism, primarySelector, whyAutomatedToolsMiss and citation all belong to a different, never-shipped page, and the selector it names does not exist in the DOM - a mechanical metadata repair, not a ground-truth question: expected='failed' is correct for the page as shipped (F103) and stays unchanged. The annotator UI already carries a selector override ('#refillStatus ... orig ... matched nothing'), independently corroborating the mismatch.

The indicator is a present, valid live region wired role=alert (assertive); a debounced handler flips it 'Saving…' -> 'All changes saved' roughly every two seconds while the student is still typing. Each flip assertively interrupts the screen reader's typing echo, so the student stops hearing their own words. An autosave confirmation is low-value and belongs in a polite region at most.",
            "expected": "failed",
            "mechanism": "role=alert is assertive: each text change interrupts current speech. While the user composes, the AT echoes their typing; every ~2s the debounced autosave flips the assertive region twice ('Saving…' then 'All changes saved'), each flip preempting the typing echo (verified by MutationObserver capturing both transitions during active typing). The information is low-value, high-cadence — it should be polite (role=status). Valid markup, wrong politeness.",
